description: Dead-man's switch for the flap monitor itself. The monitor's error path (script failure, SUPERVISOR_TOKEN loss, log-fetch failure) lands binary_sensor.cameras_flapping in 'unavailable'; without this automation that state is terminal-silent. 60 min clears benign windows (HA/Scrypted restarts recover in 5-15 min). NOTE (corrected 2026-08-17, updated 2026-10-14): a cam_health death does NOT trip this - the window is measured from log timestamps, and cam_vision.py fetches the 9 endpoints itself once cam_health's shared frames go stale; cam_health's own dead-man is camera_health_monitor_down. RE-ASSERTS hourly (:47) while the sensor stays dead (restart-wipe guard). (2026-10-10: the unavailable/unknown hold is an OR of single-state conditions with for:, because HA 2026.10 rejects for: with a list of states.) 2026-10-28: START-UP CHECK. A state trigger needs a change after it attaches, so a monitor that was already dead when Home Assistant started (a Core update, or a deploy followed by a restart, that breaks the script) never fired this alert, and the re-assert restores the card without a push. On the start trigger the run now waits up to 60 min for the monitor to be healthy and pages if it is not; its push says the fault has been present since the start, because the check repeats, once per start, a page sent before the restart. The check runs only on a Home Assistant start: an automation reload that re-arms the triggers while the fault is present is not covered. camera_monitor_stalled pushes an unchanging error, or an unknown state, at about the same time (45-min bar plus its 15-min hold).

then.stop: the monitor was healthy at the start or recovered within the hold
